Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Phase 3 of NxLabs (the mod/plugin catalog). This task: build a real mod.io-based import pipeline, following the exact conventions of the existing Modrinth pipeline.

## Context you need
- A real, valid mod.io developer API key now exists at `/opt/nxeon/.env` and `/opt/nxeon-staging/.env` as `MODIO_API_KEY` — confirmed live moments ago via `https://api.mod.io/v1/games?api_key=...`. This is a genuine developer account key (owner signed mod.io's terms directly), not a per-game key — check the real rate-limit headers on your actual API responses (`X-RateLimit-*` or similar) to confirm the real limit for THIS key type rather than assuming the "unlimited with game-linked key" figure from earlier research, which may not apply to a general developer key.
- `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts` is the reference pattern: dry-run by default behind `scripts/db-target-guard.ts`, upserts on `GameMod`'s `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])`, idempotent (safe to re-run, must produce `created=0` on a second run). Read it in full before writing anything.
- `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `GameMod` model — check current exact fields (has grown since Phase 1: now includes `galleryUrls`, `authorName`, `authorAvatarUrl`, `longDescription` as of tonight).
- Legal/data policy: mod.io mods have no per-mod license field in the API (verify live, don't assume) — treat as FETCH-AT-INSTALL-TIME ONLY like Thunderstore/Steam Workshop, never mirror the actual file into our own storage. Real icon/gallery images ARE available via their API (`logo`, `media.images[]`) — use them, they're legitimately part of the API response.
- Games to import, using the real mod.io game IDs (query `GET /v1/games?api_key=...` yourself and match by name — don't guess IDs): **Core Keeper**, **Space Engineers**, **Insurgency: Sandstorm**, **Mordhau** — these 4 were confirmed to have live mod.io presence in earlier research this session. Match Nxeon's own `gameFamily` keys from `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_CONTROL` (`corekeeper`, `spaceengineers`, `sandstorm`, `mordhau`).
- Apply a real quality gate similar to Modrinth's (document your threshold and why, e.g. a minimum download-count floor).

## CRITICAL process rule from tonight's incident
**Multiple agents running their own `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` concurrently corrupted BOTH staging and production's `.next` build output tonight and caused a real production outage.** It's fixed now, but do not repeat it.

**Do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, poll every 30s until clear before you even begin. This task is primarily a DATA import (like Modrinth's bulk import, which needed no rebuild since pages are `force-dynamic`) — if you only add/run an import script and don't touch `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `resolveUrl()`/`RESOLVABLE_SOURCES`, no deploy is needed at all, just run the import directly against the live DB. If you DO need to add mod.io as a new resolvable source (check `lib/mod-install-support.ts`), make that code change, commit and push it, but do NOT deploy — say so explicitly in your report and I'll deploy it along with other pending work.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, and `lib/mod-install-support.ts` in full first.
- DB reads/writes only via `db` from `lib/db`, scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` via `npx tsx`, delete when done. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string — a staging DB password already leaked once tonight from a careless `.env` cat, don't repeat that.
- Dry-run first, verify sane sample output per game, then `--apply`, then re-run once to confirm idempotency (`created=0` second time).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean if you touched any app code.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Commit and push to `main` if you changed code (check `git log origin/main` before/after for concurrent pushes). If it's pure data population with no code changes, nothing to commit — just report the real import numbers.

Report back: real counts imported per game, the quality-gate threshold chosen and why, the actual rate limit you observed for this key, confirmation of idempotency, and whether any code change (thus a pending deploy) resulted.

# mod.io API Rate Limits for API Keys

Based on the documentation, here are the rate limits for API key authentication:

## Rate Limit Details

**Global API Key Rate Limiting:**
- "API keys linked to a game have **unlimited requests**."
- "API keys linked to a user have **60 requests per minute**."

## Header Deprecation

The documentation includes an important notice about response headers:

"From November 20th, 2022 - the rate limit headers below will no longer be returned. If you have written a custom mod.io SDK or library, you should replace any usage of these headers with `retry-after`."

The deprecated headers were:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`
- `X-RateLimit-RetryAfter`

## Current Approach

Modern implementations should rely on the `retry-after` header returned with `429 Too Many Requests` responses instead of the older `X-RateLimit-*` headers, which are no longer documented as being returned.

---

## 2026-09-20 — NxLabs Phase 3: real mod.io import (Core Keeper, Space Engineers, Insurgency: Sandstorm, Mordhau)

**`scripts/import-modio-catalog.ts` (new, permanent, re-runnable).** Same shape as
`scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`/`scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts`: dry-run by default,
`scripts/db-target-guard.ts` enforced, idempotent `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` upsert (matched by
real immutable `sourceId` = mod.io's numeric mod id, since mod.io's `name_id` slug can be renamed by
the author — same pattern as `scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`, not Modrinth's plain-slug one).

**Real mod.io game ids** (checked live against `GET /v1/games`, matched by name to `lib/games.ts`):
Core Keeper=5289 → `corekeeper`, Space Engineers=264 → `spaceengineers`, Insurgency: Sandstorm=254 →
`sandstorm`, MORDHAU=169 → `mordhau`.

**Rate limit — checked live, not assumed.** The `MODIO_API_KEY` in `.env` returns
`x-modio-key: user` on every response — mod.io's own header naming it a USER-linked developer-account
key. mod.io's docs are explicit the "unlimited requests" tier is GAME-linked keys only; a user-linked
key is documented at 60 req/min. No `X-RateLimit-*` headers are returned at all (mod.io dropped them
platform-wide in Nov 2022 in favor of `retry-after` on real 429s) — confirmed empirically too: a
60-request burst in ~26s returned zero 429s and no rate-limit headers of any kind. Script self-paces
at 50/min (a margin under the documented 60/min ceiling) rather than trusting the absence of headers
as "unlimited."

**License — verified live, not assumed.** A real mod object (Core Keeper's top mod, "CoreLib") was
inspected field-by-field: no `license` key exists anywhere in mod.io's API. `license` is always
written `null`, matching the established Thunderstore/Steam Workshop precedent for sources with no
license concept. Real icon (`logo`) and gallery (`media.images[]`) CDN images ARE used — legitimately
part of the public API response. No mod file is ever downloaded/mirrored by this script; the real file
is fetched by the worker at install time, same as every other source (see the open gap below — that
mechanism doesn't exist yet for any of these 4 families).

**Quality gate: `downloads_total > 1000`** — the same numeric floor `import-modrinth-catalog.ts`
uses. Checked live where it lands: corekeeper 194/312, sandstorm 560/773, mordhau 801/1435. Tried a
Modrinth-style disjoint second pass on `subscribers_total` (the follows-analogue) first — checked live
how many rows it would add beyond the downloads floor for all 4 games: corekeeper 0, sandstorm 0,
mordhau 1, spaceengineers 0. Not a real gain; not implemented, per the same finding
`import-thunderstore-catalog.ts` already documented for `rating_score`.

**Space Engineers needed an extra content-type filter, Modrinth-`environment`-style.** Its mod.io
catalogue is 165,922 items but 87% (144,710) are `Blueprint`-tagged personal ship designs — not server
mod content at all. Real per-tag totals checked live: Blueprint 144,710, World 16,945, ingameScript
744, scenario 37, **Mod 3,113** — only `tags=Mod` is genuinely "install this on my dedicated server"
content (loaded via the game's real `Mods=` list). This script imports `tags=Mod` only for Space
Engineers; the 1000-download floor then lands at 1,170/3,113. The other 3 games' tag taxonomies have
no comparable non-installable majority bucket (checked live) so no equivalent filter applies to them.

**Category** derived from each game's own live tag taxonomy (`GET /v1/games/{id}/tags`), not
fabricated: corekeeper from its "Type" group (Visual/Audio/Item/NPC/QoL/Overhaul/Language/Library),
sandstorm from its "Mods" group (Total Conversion/Custom Theater/Game Mode/Mutator — a map with no
such tag keeps the family's real `ugc_name` "Mods" since Sandstorm draws no client/server distinction
between maps and mods), mordhau from its "Type" group (Map/Skin/Serverside Only/Dependency/Admin
Tool/Item Removal/RCON/Audio/Misc). Space Engineers rows are trivially "Mod" (already filtered).
`gameVersions` and a real `serverSide` (Client/Server tag → unsupported/required) are populated only
for Core Keeper, the one game of the 4 whose live taxonomy actually carries those facets — verified,
not guessed, for the other 3.

**Real, verified import counts (production, 2026-09-20):** corekeeper 194, spaceengineers 1,170,
sandstorm 560, mordhau 801. **2,725 real rows total, 0 failures.** Re-run twice on staging and twice
on production; both second runs returned `created=0, updated=2725` — confirmed idempotent.

**Known gap, documented rather than silently left.** Checked `lib/mod-install-support.ts`: none of
corekeeper/spaceengineers/sandstorm/mordhau are in `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` today, so every imported row
renders "install it yourself in Files" regardless of source. Since the family gate fails before the
source gate is ever checked, adding `mod_io` to `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` would have had zero visible
effect for any of these 4 families — deliberately NOT done this pass. Real per-family config-write
mechanisms (how each of these 4 dedicated servers actually takes a mod.io id) are unresearched,
separate follow-up work, not bundled into a pure catalogue-population pass.

**No app code required a deploy.** The only application-code touches were `prisma/schema.prisma`'s
`source` field doc comment (added `mod_io` to the listed values — comment only, no migration) and
`lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s `SOURCE_LABEL` map (added `mod_io: "mod.io"`, a display-string fallback that
already degrades gracefully to the raw string). Neither touches `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `resolveUrl()`
or `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES`, so nothing here needs the next deploy to be safe or correct — the
`SOURCE_LABEL` entry just won't render as "mod.io" (falls back to "mod_io") in the admin catalogue
view until the next normal deploy picks it up.
